details.publicNotes:
Ugadalus, also known as root walkers, are sadistic creatures comprised of gnarled wood with large masks for faces. According to legend, the first ugadalu was a warrior whose soul was bound to his mask after a grisly ritual, though how they've since grown into an entire species of creature is unclear. Did the first ugadalu perform the same ritual on others? Or did the spell, once performed, plough a furrow in the world's magic, making it easier for similar creatures to occur naturally?

Ugadalus subjugate small settlements and rule through terror. They respond violently to anything that would dare to threaten their dominion. An ugadalu doesn't care for the identity of this intruder. Instead, they treat all invaders equally, whether they are dangerous monsters on the prowl or heroes seeking to free the people from tyranny. When not actively issuing commands to those they bully and intimidate, ugadalus spend much of their time in the form of wooden statues, preparing to ambush and frighten whoever is unfortunate enough to walk by. In battle, ugadalus unleash a continuous stream of flowing fire from their open mouths, which they can flare into a powerful burst of flame and spew at their foes.

Though they enjoy inflicting fear upon others, ironically, ugadalus can't bear the experience of being afraid themselves. Not only that, what they fear more than anything else lies buried deep within their own natures. As such, they are rattled by the sight of others of their kind, and even their own reflections are intolerable.

No Self-Reflection

Ugadalus relish their roles as rulers of their small domains. They issue sweeping decrees, both for the joy of watching others do their bidding and for the thrill of punishing those who stubbornly—or unwittingly—disobey. Some of the most common ugadalu laws are the banning of reflective surfaces: mirrors must be shattered, silver melted, and clear ponds muddied or emptied. Some go further and order the destruction of all writing implements, on the grounds that they could be used to draw a representation of an ugadalu.

You force the target to see a vision of its own death. It takes 8d6 mental damage with a Will save. If the target is reduced to 0 HP by this spell, its vision becomes reality and kills it instantly.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target takes half damage and is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The target takes full damage and is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure The target takes double damage, is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 4} and is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for as long as it's frightened.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 2d6.

You plant fear in the target; it must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} and @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for 1 round.

Heightened (3rd) You can target up to five creatures.

An ugadalu is their own worst nightmare. When an ugadalu starts their turn frightened, they take @Damage[1d8[mental]] damage. If an ugadalu that was not already frightened sees an ugadalu within 30 feet, whether it be another ugadalu, a creature wearing an ugadalu's mask, or a clear reflection of their own face, the ugadalu becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}. While within 30 feet of this fearful sight, the ugadalu can't reduce the value of their frightened condition below 1.

Trigger A creature moves within 30 feet of the ugadalu while the ugadalu is in Statue Form

Requirements Initiative has not yet been rolled

Effect The ugadalu attempts an Intimidation check to @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.2u915NdUyQan6uKF]{Demoralize} the triggering creature, using their Intimidation result for their initiative.
The ugadalu's jaws Strike deals an additional 2d6 precision damage to frightened creatures.

The ugadalu concentrates their stream of fire and emits a burst of flames that deals @Damage[8d6[fire]|options:area-damage] damage in a @Template[type:cone|distance:30] (@Check[reflex|dc:25|basic] save). They can't use Spew Flame again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Spew Flame]]{1d4 rounds}.

The ugadalu transforms, taking the form of a wooden statue of a warrior. Perception checks don't typically reveal the ugadalu's true nature, but a creature who examines the statue attempts a secret @Check[crafting|dc:25] check; on a success, they are able to determine that the statue is alive. While in statue form, an ugadalu can observe everything around them, but they can't receive a result better than a failure on Reflex save, so if they roll a success or critical success, they get a failure instead. They can't act other to Dismiss this effect or use Jump Scare.
